record.paper_title: Unfolding the Labyrinth: Open Problems in Physics, Mathematics, Astrophysics and Other Areas of Science
record.original_question: Is it possible to partition the positive integers into infinitely many arbitrary classes in such a way that at least one class contains an arithmetic progression of length l with l > 3, and if so what is the maximum value of l for which this remains true?

evidence.quote: Expanding to infinity van der Waerden’s theorem: Is it possible to partition N* into an infinity of arbitrary classes such that at least one class contains an arithmetic progression of l terms ( l >3)?  Find the maximum l having this property.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Van der Waerden's theorem states that for every finite coloring of the positive integers $\mathbb{N}^{*}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$, at least one color class contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. Consider now partitions of $\mathbb{N}^{*}$ into infinitely many nonempty classes $\mathbb{N}^{*}=\bigsqcup_{i\in\mathbb{N}} A_i$ (with no restriction on the classes other than that they form a partition).

(a) Does there exist an integer $\ell>3$ such that, for every partition of $\mathbb{N}^{*}$ into infinitely many classes, at least one class $A_i$ contains an arithmetic progression of length $\ell$?

(b) If such integers $\ell$ exist, determine the largest one — i.e., find
$$\ell^{*}=\sup\{\ell\in\mathbb{N}: \text{every partition of }\mathbb{N}^{*}\text{ into infinitely many classes has some class containing an AP of length }\ell\}.$$
In particular, decide whether $\ell^{*}$ is finite or infinite.
artifact.status_search_result: A direct construction shows that one can partition $\mathbb{N}^{*}$ into infinitely many classes none of which contains any 3-term arithmetic progression (e.g., place each integer in its own singleton class), so the naive form of the question is trivial. The intended non-trivial formulation (with some implicit regularity constraint on the classes) does not appear to have a definitive resolution in the literature, and no widely cited solution could be located. The status is therefore taken to be unknown.

status_evidence.title: Van der Waerden's theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Van der Waerden's theorem concerns finite colorings of the integers; extensions to infinite partitions require additional density or structure hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Classical van der Waerden theorem is stated for finite colorings; the infinite-class extension is not a standard theorem.
